name: JARRETT, Madonna

headline.note: First-person parliamentary speech explicitly supports a full-time working career from age17, apart from a six-month parental break. Employer and date evidence is still incomplete, including radiography sector, departmental versus consultancy periods, early Deloitte roles and the placement of leave. Almost25 corporate years is an approximate career description, not a calculated sector total. No unsupported duration or zero encoded.

The official biography records work as a radiographer and the ALP biography says Jarrett started her career in health. Employer, jurisdiction, dates, hours, leave and public/private control are not published. Personal speech establishes full-time radiography. Profile lead identifies Mater cadetship followed by private practice1984–1989; primary hospital/employer confirmation and split dates needed. Sector remains unknown.

The offices, employing entities, dates, hours and leave remain unpublished.
career_spells.counting_note: Personal first-speech full-time statement supports status, but role boundaries, sector allocation and placement of six-month parental break remain unresolved; no total calculated.

career_spells.role: Global public relations / chief-executive communications role
career_spells.evidence_note: Jarrett's ALP biography describes a 25-year private-sector career. A contemporary Deloitte release identifies her as Director, Global Public Relations and CEO Communications on 19 December 2005; later releases again identify the global public-relations role in January 2006 and list her as a Deloitte media contact in 2007 and 2008. A public professional-profile aggregation places the next Deloitte program-lead role from September 2010. The original Deloitte commencement date, legal employing entity, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Personal first-speech full-time statement supports status, but role boundaries, sector allocation and placement of six-month parental break remain unresolved; no total calculated.

career_spells.role: Program Lead, Global Regulatory and Public Policy Group / Global Public Policy Group
career_spells.evidence_note: A public professional-profile aggregation reports Global Regulatory and Public Policy program leadership from September 2010 to October 2014 and Global Public Policy program leadership from October 2014 to September 2017. A 2017 IOE/Deloitte report independently identifies Jarrett as a Director of Deloitte Belgium and the Deloitte Global Public Policy Group, corroborating employer and function but not the full month sequence or hours. Association-hosted March2015 joint release supplies an earlier contemporaneous Deloitte Global Public Policy Group observation, without endorsing aggregation-only boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: Personal first-speech full-time statement supports status, but role boundaries, sector allocation and placement of six-month parental break remain unresolved; no total calculated.

career_spells.role: Acting Chief of Staff, then Chief of Staff, Global Risk and Regulatory / Public Policy leadership
career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional-profile aggregations report Acting Chief of Staff from September 2017 to June 2018 and Chief of Staff from June 2018 to January 2019. A 2018 Deloitte-supported report independently identifies Jarrett as a director in Deloitte's Global Risk and Regulatory Group in Belgium, corroborating the organisation and senior global-risk function but not payroll conditions.
career_spells.counting_note: Personal first-speech full-time statement supports status, but role boundaries, sector allocation and placement of six-month parental break remain unresolved; no total calculated.

career_spells.role: Director, Global Risk and Global Regulatory and Public Policy / Strategy, Innovation and Public Policy
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography confirms Deloitte employment. ABC's 2022 and 2025 election guides identify Jarrett's most recent role as a Deloitte Australia director responsible for global risk and regulatory/public policy. A public professional-profile aggregation gives January 2019 as the start, and news profiles report her return to Australia in 2019 after about 15 years overseas. An August 2023 joint IOE-Deloitte report names her as Director, Strategy, Innovation and Public Policy, Deloitte Global, establishing a later dated employer observation and title evolution but not continuous service, hours or a cessation boundary. Withdrawn synthetic day-before-election end; actual cessation/campaign leave unknown. First speech supplies full-time status but not payroll boundaries or parental-break dates.
career_spells.counting_note: Personal first-speech full-time statement supports status, but role boundaries, sector allocation and placement of six-month parental break remain unresolved; no total calculated.

career_spells.counting_note: Volunteer governance is excluded from substantive employment totals.

research_notes: Identify the radiography employer, dates, hours and whether it was publicly or privately controlled.

Identify each NSW and Queensland ministerial office, employing entity, title, appointment/cessation, hours and leave; confirm whether any role was public-service employment rather than political staff.

Obtain a primary Deloitte appointment history: original commencement, legal employing entities, movements between Australia and Belgium, exact title boundaries, hours, leave and final cessation or campaign arrangement.

The public professional-profile aggregations provide useful month-level leads but are not treated as proof of full-time status or uninterrupted payroll service. Seek archived Deloitte biographies, annual reports and conference profiles.

Resolve whether any other paid employment occurred between radiography, government advisory work and Deloitte, and distinguish public affairs or crisis-management consulting from internal Deloitte roles.

2026-10-02 follow-up: recovered explicit full-time and six-month leave evidence, MJM Issues Management consultancy and separate departmental-unit role from historical ministerial records; board annual-report corroboration. Profile leads additionally identify Queensland Justice/Corrective Services adviser1989–1990, Queensland Employment/Training/IR adviser/chief of staff1992–1996 and NSW vocational education adviser1996–1998; verify offices and true dates before splitting existing grouped row. Radiography Mater/private practice1984–1989 and Victorian Financial Institutions Commission1991–1992 require primary records. Early Deloitte2000–2004 roles added as provisional; Jan boundaries not asserted. Original global role may begin September2004 (aggregation), to corroborate against employer archive. No calculation until dates, overlaps and six-month leave placement resolved. Annual-report2022–23 full open400 size error was source-only; indexed passage and accessible2023–24 report used. Search namesakes Dr Anderson/SPI Pharma rejected. Do not infer an unbroken25-year total or literal2000 appointment from opposition assertion corrected by minister.
Validation caught pre-existing governance category outside approved vocabulary; volunteer board row recoded unpaid_work, still excluded. Local AssertionError resolved before commit.

2026-10-03 follow-up: an August 2023 joint IOE-Deloitte report provides the latest primary Deloitte observation found and records a title change to Director, Strategy, Innovation and Public Policy, Deloitte Global. It does not establish uninterrupted service from January 2019, weekly hours, campaign leave or final cessation. Fresh Queensland parliamentary, Mater, historical government-office and Deloitte searches otherwise repeated existing facts or professional-profile aggregations; exact early employers and boundaries remain unresolved.

2026-10-04 follow-up: a contemporary Deloitte IAS Plus release identifies Jarrett as Director, Global Public Relations and CEO Communications on 19 December 2005, moving the first primary Deloitte observation earlier than the January 2006 release. Exact-name searches for Mater radiography, the Victorian Financial Institutions Commission and Queensland Justice/Corrective Services produced only professional-profile aggregations already treated as leads, not original appointment or payroll evidence. Early employers, government-office boundaries, hours, the six-month parental break placement and Deloitte commencement remain unresolved.

Targeted follow-up2026-10-05: Added previously unseparated intermittent1995Aspley and2022/2025Brisbane candidacy, primary1999 parliamentary report corroborating the earlier contest. No continuous party job or campaign-induced Deloitte cessation inferred. Earlier Deloitte2001 query exposed only professional aggregations. Full-name/Madonna Camp historical search yielded no primary radiography, VFIC or ministerial personnel boundary. Original2000 Hansard identifies the alternative name, but its disputed current-job claim remains superseded by Braddy's correction. Next: hospital/vintage government personnel lists or original Deloitte role/leave records.

Targeted second follow-up2026-10-05: primary BusinessNZ/BIAC March2015 release corroborates Deloitte public-policy function and adds previously missing BIACcommittee vice-chair, excluded governance. Deloitte reportlink redirects with500/non-retryable sourceerror; no unseen report facts used. WebWire2005release independently repeats already-supported19December2005 role, not earlier start. CorporateWiki NewYorkdirector entry is a possible historicalfiling lead, not proof of personal payroll entity or employment. Mater/privatepractice,VFIC,government offices and parental-break placement remain unresolved.
